turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Hi, I'm Dr.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Hadad.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Can you confirm your full name and date of birth for me?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thomas Kowalsik, May 3rd, 1981.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thanks, Thomas. You're walking a little carefully there.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: What happened?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Yes,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Saturday I was helping move pallets at work, and I picked up a box of floor tile wrong. Twisted, you know, felt something grab in my lower back, right side.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Out, where do you work again?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Harbor Point Distribution. I'm a shift laid in the warehouse. house. Got it on a scale of zero to ten. How bad is the pain? Right now, maybe a six. When I bend over to tie my shoes, it's like an eight.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Does it go anywhere,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: like down your leg? A little into the right butt cheek, not down the leg.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any numbness or tingling in your legs or feet. Any weakness, like your foot dragging.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, no numbness.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Legs feel normal just the back. I have to ask a few important ones. Any numbness in the groin or between your legs, like where you'd sit on a saddle.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any trouble controlling your bladder or bowels, or trouble starting to pee?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, everything's working fine there. Any fevers,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: unexplained weight loss, or any history of cancer?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: None of that. Have you had back trouble before? I had sciatica on the left side maybe six years ago. Did physical therapy, and it went away completely, haven't had it since.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: what have you tried so far? I be profan two of the two hundreds a couple times a day, and my wife Agneske's heating pad. The heat helps some. I'm kind of worried though, a guy on my crew herniated a disc doing the same thing and needed surgery. That's understandable.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let's take a look. 98 .4. Can you stand and bend forward for me?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's about as far as I go.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, forward bending is limited by pain,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: about halfway.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I can feel tight, tender muscles along the right side of your lower back. No tenderness when I press right on the spine itself.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Now lie back.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'm going to raise each leg straight.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Just pulls in the back a little.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Straight leg raise is negative on both sides. Strength is normal in both legs, reflexes are equal at the knees and ankles and you can feel my touch the same on both sides. You walked in normally and you can walk on your heels and toes.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: So is it a disc?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I don't think so. This looks like a strain of the muscles in your lower back. There are no warning signs, so you don't need an X -ray or MRI right now. Most of these get a lot better in two to four weeks.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: that's a relief. For pain, take ibuprofen 600 mg three times a day with food for the next week or so. I'm also prescribing cyclobenzaprine, a muscle relaxer, 5 mg at bedtime as needed for spasm. It can make you drowsy, so no driving or running the forklift after you take it. Keep using heat and keep moving. Gentle walking is better than bed rest. I'll write you a note for light duty, no lifting over 20 pounds, through October 15th.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My supervisor will want that, thanks.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: If you're not better in two weeks, come back and we'll start physical therapy. And if you ever lose control of your bladder or bowels, get numb between your legs, or a leg gets weak, go to the emergency room right away. Okay,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: hopefully it doesn't come to that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I don't expect it to. Let's plan a follow -up in two weeks.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Take care of that back, Thomas.
